description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and various accuracy metrics, including Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, and tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents Accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy (blue, solid line with square markers), Δ Accuracy (orange, dashed line with diamond markers), and Initial Accuracy (green, dash-dot line with square markers). The Final Accuracy line remains relatively stable, starting at approximately 0.97 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81 and ending at around 0.96 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some fluctuations in between, such as a dip to 0.86 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86. The Δ Accuracy line starts at around 0.4 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, decreases to approximately 0.16 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, and then continues to decline to around 0.07 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some fluctuations. The Initial Accuracy line begins at approximately 0.52 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, increases to around 0.72 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, and then continues to rise to approximately 0.93 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some variations in between.
